decisions.reason: F5 omitted the supplier hypothesis phi composed with f is integrable. Both uses satisfy it: the gradient is continuous on each compact segment in 1.2, and |v(x)-v(.)|^p is integrable by v in Lp(V) in 3.1. The segment substitutions, convex exhaustion, mean convergence and dimension-only constant remain valid. Corrected F5 and made both integrability checks explicit; the original Statement is unchanged.

The standalone Remark did not state n>=2, although the page convention and logarithmic witnesses do. On an interval an absolutely continuous W11 representative satisfies sup|u|<=|I|^-1||u||1+||u prime||1, by averaging |u(x)|<=|u(y)|+integral|u prime| in y. Thus the unqualified Linfinity nonembedding is false in dimension one. Added n>=2 and the precise exceptional interval bound; for n>=2 the local double-logarithm has gradient energy integral dr/(r log(R/r)^n)<infinity and essential unboundedness, giving the stated limitation.

Minkowski requires measurability for the product sigma-algebra, whereas original 2.1 established only completed-product measurability. The original invocation was therefore unsupported. Replaced it by the finite Borel representative g0 supplied by the already declared completion theorem, so k(z)g0(x-z) is product-measurable. Translation isometry gives the finite Minkowski right side. Added the existing published reflection theorem to justify x-N null for each fixed x and the convolution substitution. Kernel mass is 2rho sigma(S); the central John ball and endpoint curve estimate give the asserted volume control. The Statement is unchanged.

F2 omitted the source exponent p from the exact embedding supplier constant C(n,p,r,Omega). Corrected that fact and wrote C(n,s,q,Omega) at its use in 1.2. This is nonfatal: s=nq/(n+q) is fixed by n,q, lies in (n/2,n), and has s*=q, so the final advertised C(n,q,Omega) is licensed. Holder for all n+1 Sobolev components supplies W1s membership. The cut-off double-logarithm has finite Ln function and gradient; coordinate lines off a null transverse singleton justify the weak derivative, and positive-measure superlevels rule out a bounded sequence of constants as q tends to infinity. Statement unchanged.

F5 incorrectly described Countable Choice as a hypothesis of the cited Holder theorem, whose Statement has no choice assumption. This is a nonfatal attribution defect: the ambient AC already implies CC, and Holder applies without it. Corrected F5 and made the differentiation domain explicit by applying the Rn theorem to the zero extension of u, locally integrable by Holder. Kernel exponent n-(n-1)p prime is positive exactly for p>n and its root exponent is 1-n/p. Nested means converge at every interior point; differentiation identifies the representative almost everywhere. Overlapping means at separation <=r/2 and the fixed doubled-ball mean for larger separation give the stated bound and continuity. Statement unchanged.

F3 misstated the source constant as C_E(n,q,Omega), omitting p from the supplied C(n,p,q,Omega). Corrected F3 and also retained the scalar-field dependence K supplied by the actual mean-zero lemma in F1. This is nonfatal: the proof fixes p, takes q=p*, and its conclusion already permits C(n,p,Omega,K). The finite-measure mean is defined by Holder; centering preserves Sobolev membership and gradient, the local mean-zero lemma controls the Lp term, and the exact embedding at p* controls the full centered Sobolev norm. AC supplies the CC/DC hypotheses. Neither Statement nor Definition changed.

The two-ball witness is sound under CC: locally constant u has zero weak gradient, equal positive ball measures give mean 1/2, and centered Lp norm is |Omega|^(1/p)/2>0 for every finite p>=1. The supplemental John-domain positive contrast in original 3.1 cited an AC theorem without this extra hypothesis. This is nonfatal to the counterexample but a genuine dependency-attribution defect in the comparison. Added conditional full AC in F5 and 3.1, with the AC definition dependency, while retaining the original CC counterexample interface and its half-domain zero-set observation. Statement refuted unchanged.
